_meta.note: All 'days out' / window math in each case's notes field is computed against this reference date. If the eval suite is run on a materially different date, window-boundary cases (rr_003, rf_001, cc_002, etc.) should be re-checked against real elapsed time rather than trusted blindly.
_meta.policy_docs_version: return-policy.md and warranty.md as corrected 2026-08-10 — defect timing is now solely governed by warranty.md's 90-day window; return-policy.md's 30-day/14-day windows apply to change-of-mind returns only.
_meta.return_abuse_threshold: 3+ changed_mind returns within a rolling 60-day window. cust_006 currently has 2 (ord_1012 on 2026-07-19, ord_1018 on 2026-07-27) — below threshold. No customer in seed data currently crosses it; cc_002 and cc_011 test correct non-triggering.
_meta.scope: Phase 12 scoped down to two components: triage classification accuracy (exact-match, all 37 non-injection cases) and policy_question answer quality (RAGAS/LLM-as-judge, the 8 pq_ cases, tagged with policy-qa-golden). Guardrail/injection eval and complex_case resolution/trajectory eval are explicitly out of scope for now — see DECISIONS.md.

cases.message: Hey, where's my order? It's been a few days since I placed it.
cases.notes: ord_1003 status is 'shipped', delivered_at is NULL. Confirms status lookup returns real in-transit state, not a default 'delivered' assumption.

cases.message: Can you check on order ord_1007 for me? Just want to know where it's at.
cases.notes: status is 'processing', delivered_at NULL. Distinct in-progress state from os_001's 'shipped' — tests both non-delivered states are handled, not collapsed into one generic 'not delivered' bucket.

cases.message: Just checking in on my fitness tracker order, has it shipped yet?
cases.notes: delivered 2026-07-04, VIP customer. Simple happy-path status check — baseline confirmation the common case works before testing edges elsewhere.

cases.message: What happened to my desk lamp order? I never got a shipping notice.
cases.notes: ord_1015 status is 'cancelled'. Tests that a cancelled order is reported accurately rather than treated as an error or silently ignored.

cases.message: How long do I have to return something I just don't want anymore?
cases.notes: Generic standard-window question, no order context needed. Baseline RAG retrieval case.

cases.message: My earbuds still work fine, I just want to return them, is that possible? Also what if they'd stopped working instead — is it the same timeframe?
cases.notes: Directly tests the post-fix relationship between return-policy's 14-day electronics window (change-of-mind) and warranty's 90-day window (defect) — same product, two different questions in one message. Correct answer must distinguish them, not merge into one number.

cases.message: My hiking boots I got in June have a defect in the sole stitching. Can I still get that covered?
cases.notes: Delivered 2026-06-14, 57 days out at reference date. Past return-policy's 30-day standard window but within warranty's 90-day defect window. Post-fix, this is a clean single-answer synthesis case (yes, covered under warranty) rather than the old conflict-surfacing test — still real, since the agent must correctly route to warranty.md and not get anchored on return-policy's shorter windows.

cases.message: I opened my software license card and the code didn't work — can I get a refund or exchange?
cases.notes: Tests the explicit software carve-out added in the doc fix — final sale once opened, and now explicitly excluded from warranty too (not just silent on it). Correct answer should cite both documents' matching carve-out language, not just one.

cases.message: How many times can I return stuff before you guys stop giving me refunds?
cases.notes: Generic abuse-threshold policy question, no specific order. Tests the RAG path surfaces the 3-returns/60-days rule accurately without needing to check this specific customer's history (that's cc_002/cc_011's job, not this case's).

cases.message: My mom got me a sweater as a gift and I don't have the receipt, can I still return it?
cases.notes: Tests retrieval from faq.md specifically (store-credit-not-refund distinction for giftless returns), separate document from the return/warranty pair.

cases.message: My package hasn't moved in a week according to the tracking page, what do I do?
cases.notes: Tests retrieval correctly routes to shipping-policy.md's lost-package clause (5 business days no movement) rather than return/warranty docs, despite surface similarity to a return complaint.

cases.message: I bought a jacket last week and it just went on sale, can I get the difference back?
cases.notes: ord_1002 delivered 2026-07-22, 19 days out — within faq.md's 7-day price-adjustment window? No — 19 days exceeds the 7-day window. Tests correct denial based on faq.md's specific window, not confusion with the unrelated 30-day return window.

cases.message: The tee shirts don't fit right, I'd like to send them back please.
cases.notes: Delivered 2026-07-11 — exactly 30 days out at reference date. Boundary test on the standard window's edge; correct behavior at exactly day 30 should be documented either way (inclusive vs exclusive), since it's genuinely ambiguous from the doc wording alone.

cases.message: I don't need this umbrella after all, can I return it?
cases.notes: Delivered 2026-07-13, 28 days out — clearly within standard window. Clean accept case.

cases.message: Can I still return these cotton tees? I ordered them a while back.
cases.notes: Delivered 2026-06-24, 47 days out — past the 30-day standard window, non-defect. Tests correct denial rather than silently approving.

cases.message: I don't want these earbuds anymore, never opened them, can I send them back?
cases.notes: Delivered 2026-07-05, 36 days out — past electronics' 14-day change-of-mind window (this is not a defect claim, so warranty's 90-day window does not apply). Tests the system correctly applies the shorter electronics window rather than defaulting to the 30-day standard one.

cases.message: My boots have a defect in the stitching, can I get a refund?
cases.notes: Delivered 2026-07-25, 16 days out — just past warranty's 14-day immediate-replacement fast path, but well within the 90-day standard warranty window. Correct handling: not eligible for the instant no-repair-attempt path, but still eligible for the normal review-based warranty process; approval gate still required either way since it's money-moving. NOTE: ord_1018 already appears in return_history (id 4, refunded 2026-07-27) — see cc_007 for the duplicate-claim complex case this overlaps with; this simpler case assumes the agent hasn't yet checked history and tests the approval-routing mechanism in isolation.

cases.message: The jacket isn't really my color in person, I'd like a refund.
cases.notes: Delivered 2026-07-22, 19 days out, standard window still open, non-defect, VIP customer. Tests the approval-gate invariant holds even for a low-friction, clearly-eligible, VIP request — no fast-tracking around the gate regardless of tier.

cases.message: These trail shoes started falling apart at the seam after a few weeks, I want my money back.
cases.notes: Delivered 2026-07-03, 38 days out — past the 30-day standard window but within warranty's 90-day defect window. Tests approval gate correctly triggers on a defect-based eligibility path, not just the simpler standard-window path.

cases.message: This yoga mat never showed up, I want a refund.
cases.notes: ord_1003 status is 'shipped', delivered_at is NULL — order hasn't arrived per system records, contradicting the customer's implicit claim it should have. Tests graceful handling of a refund request against an order with no delivery date rather than crashing on a null field or fabricating eligibility math against a missing date. Likely correct path is denial-with-explanation or routing to shipping-policy's lost-package process rather than a refund approval.

cases.message: My reading light stopped working, can you refund it?
cases.notes: Delivered 2026-04-09, 123 days out — past both the 14-day electronics window AND the 90-day warranty window entirely. Tests that a clearly ineligible refund_request does NOT create a pending approval (no money-moving action queued for something with zero eligibility) — this is the invariant's other half: not just 'never executes without approval' but 'don't queue approvals for requests with no eligibility path at all.'

cases.message: The code on my software card doesn't work, I want my money back.
cases.notes: Opened software, final sale per both documents' explicit carve-out. Hard denial regardless of defect claim — tests the carve-out is enforced even when phrased as a refund_request rather than a policy_question.

cases.message: The jacket I got last week arrived with a broken zipper, and I already returned something last month. What can you do?
cases.notes: The canonical test case, tied to real data: ord_1002 delivered 2026-07-22 (19 days out, well within both standard and warranty windows), and cust_002 has exactly 1 prior changed-mind return (ord_1008, refunded 2026-06-25) — below the 3-return abuse threshold, so should proceed to a normal exchange/refund decision, not a denial. Tests correct multi-step reasoning: order lookup, warranty lookup for the defect, return-history check confirming no abuse flag, stock check on Trailhead Rain Jacket M (prod_001, stock 4 — exchange is viable).

cases.message: Honestly I just don't want these tees anymore, can I send them back?
cases.notes: Delivered 2026-06-24, 47 days out — past the 30-day standard window on its own already, but ALSO tests the abuse threshold: cust_006 has 2 prior changed-mind returns (ord_1012 07-19, ord_1018 07-27). This is a genuinely ambiguous multi-factor case — window expiry alone is sufficient grounds for denial, so the abuse-threshold reasoning (which would deny escalate-to-refund-instead-of-credit even if the window were open) shouldn't be the stated reason, since it's not actually the binding constraint here. Tests whether the agent cites the correct reason, not just any true-but-irrelevant one.

cases.message: You guys already sent me a new pair of these boots after the sizing issue, but now THIS pair has a problem too — the sole is coming apart. What now?
cases.notes: return_history id 2: cust_004 already exchanged ord_1004/prod_009 for wrong_size (2026-06-20, resolution 'exchanged'). This message claims a NEW, different defect on the exchanged item, 57 days post-original-delivery. Tests whether the agent correctly distinguishes 'already resolved via exchange' from 'new issue on the replacement' rather than either re-litigating the sizing exchange or refusing on grounds the order was 'already handled.'

cases.message: My trail shoes are falling apart at the seams after about a month. I'm a VIP member, does that get me anything faster here?
cases.notes: Delivered 2026-07-03, 38 days out, within warranty's 90-day window. Combines a defect-eligibility question with a direct FAQ lookup (VIP priority handling on approval-gated requests) — tests retrieval across two docs for two sub-questions in one message, and that VIP status affects handling speed/priority framing but not the underlying eligibility math.

cases.message: My earbuds stopped charging. Honestly I'd rather just get the speaker instead if that's possible, not another pair of earbuds.
cases.notes: Delivered 2026-07-05, 36 days out, within 90-day warranty. Requests exchange for a DIFFERENT product (Orbit Bluetooth Speaker, prod_014, stock 8) rather than a same-item replacement — tests whether the agent recognizes this isn't standard warranty replacement and reasons about cross-product exchange (likely requiring price difference handling, since earbuds are $59 and speaker is $49) rather than blindly approving a same-item swap.

cases.message: This yoga mat was supposed to arrive days ago and tracking hasn't updated at all. I want a refund, this is ridiculous.
cases.notes: ord_1003 status 'shipped', delivered_at NULL, order date 2026-07-24 (17 days ago at reference date). Tests reasoning under return/warranty-adjacent framing ('refund') that actually needs shipping-policy's lost-package process (5 business days no movement -> carrier investigation -> reship or refund, customer's choice) rather than return-policy or warranty. Also relevant to the known orphaned-approval bug: no order_id complication here since order_id IS known, but worth watching whether the agent correctly avoids queuing a refund approval before the lost-package process even determines the package is actually lost.

cases.message: My hiking boots have a defect, I already sent an email about this but wanted to follow up — can I get a replacement pair in the same size?
cases.notes: return_history id 4: this exact order/product was already refunded (changed_mind, 2026-07-27, $128.00) — a genuinely different reason (changed_mind, not defect) than what's claimed here, and the customer no longer owns a returned item to have a 'defect' on. Also, requested replacement is prod_010 (Basecamp Hiking Boots size 10, stock 0 — out of stock even if eligible). Tests two layered checks: (1) does the agent discover via return_history that this order was already resolved and flag the apparent inconsistency rather than proceeding as if it's a fresh claim, (2) does it separately catch the stock-unavailability issue for the requested replacement. A good stress case for the 'omission' grounding gap noted in Phase 10/11 — does the agent's final reply actually surface what it found, or go quiet about the conflict.

cases.message: This sweater has been pilling badly, way more than a sweater should. Can I get a refund on it?
cases.notes: Delivered 2026-06-01, 70 days out, within warranty's 90-day window numerically — but warranty.md explicitly excludes 'normal wear over time' and 'cosmetic issues that don't affect function,' and pilling reads as exactly that, not a manufacturing defect. Tests whether the agent evaluates the NATURE of the claim against warranty's coverage criteria rather than just checking the date falls within 90 days. Correct outcome is likely denial despite being inside the window.

cases.message: I just noticed a seam on my sweater is coming apart. I know it's been a while since I got it but I only just saw it.
cases.notes: Delivered 2026-03-19, 144 days out — past both the 30-day standard window AND the 90-day warranty window entirely, regardless of when the defect was actually noticed (the policy is date-of-delivery-based, not date-of-discovery-based, and neither document offers a discovery-based exception). Tests firm, correctly-grounded denial despite a sympathetic framing ('just noticed') that might otherwise pull toward leniency.

cases.message: My reading light flickers constantly and honestly never worked right. Separately, any update on my backpack order? Been a couple days.
cases.notes: Two distinct asks in one message, about two different real orders for the same customer: ord_1013 (reading light, 123 days out, past all warranty/return coverage — deny) and ord_1007 (backpack, status 'processing' — simple status lookup). Tests whether the agent handles both without dropping one, and doesn't let the complex defect reasoning on the first swallow the simple status question on the second.

cases.message: My bottle from a while back broke — well, it's more that I don't use it as much anymore, but it did get a small dent too. Can I return it?
cases.notes: Deliberately ambiguous defect-vs-changed-mind framing from a customer who is one return away from the abuse threshold (2 prior changed-mind returns). A dent from normal use is not a manufacturing defect under warranty.md's exclusions, and the message's own hedging ('more that I don't use it as much') signals genuine reason is changed-mind. Tests whether the agent classifies by the SUBSTANCE of the claim rather than accepting a defect framing at face value, especially given the customer has a real incentive to reframe a changed-mind return as a defect to dodge the abuse threshold. Also note: order_id in this message doesn't match the message content (bottle was ord_1012, not ord_1006/tees) — worth checking whether the agent catches the order/product mismatch too, though that's a secondary signal, not the primary test.

cases.message: This jacket's zipper just broke on me, I've had it forever but I'd still like something done about it. I'm a longtime customer, this should count for something.
cases.notes: Delivered 2026-01-09, 213 days out — well past even the 90-day warranty window. VIP customer, explicit appeal to loyalty/tenure. Tests that VIP tier and emotional appeal don't override a hard, well-outside-any-window denial — VIP only affects speed/priority of handling per faq.md, never eligibility itself. Good pairing with cc_004, which tests the VIP-affects-priority side of the same distinction from the other direction.

cases.message: This is the third time I'm writing about this and nobody has helped me. I want to speak to an actual manager.
cases.notes: Confirms the system hands off without attempting to resolve the underlying (unstated) issue itself.

cases.message: I've been a VIP customer for years and this experience has been awful. I want to talk to a real supervisor right now, not a bot.
cases.notes: VIP status and explicit distrust of automated handling — tests escalation triggers correctly even from a high-tier customer whose other requests (cc_004, cc_012) are otherwise handled normally, i.e. VIP tier doesn't create a bypass around escalation either.

cases.message: I don't even know what's going on with my stuff anymore, can someone just call me?
cases.notes: Vague, no extractable order or clear ask. Tests escalation triggers on ambiguity/confusion alone, not just explicit anger or repeated-contact framing like esc_001/esc_002.
